text:
Gilbert Public Schools board reviews early literacy and revised budget at August meeting
S. C. Bowen
Gilbert Public Schools held a Work Study and Brief Board Business Meeting on Aug. 11, 2026, beginning at 6:00 pm in the Governing Board meeting room. All board members were present for the session, and the agenda was approved as outlined without modification.
During the meeting, Tyler Dumas, Assistant Superintendent of Teaching and Learning; Robert Bircher, Executive Director of Curriculum, Instruction and Assessment Elementary; and Cheryl Pollack, Director of Federal Affairs and State Reporting, presented on 'Early Literacy and Student Support Specialists.' Crystal Zachary, Assistant Superintendent of Business Services, presented '2026/27 Revised Budget #1.'
A link to view the August 11 Governing Board Meeting is available on YouTube.
Gilbert Public Schools operates 39 schools that serve over 32,000 students across campuses in both the Town of Gilbert and the City of Mesa. The district promotes student growth through supportive communities that foster skills for community contributions. It aims to inspire excellence in children from preschool through twelfth grade within a supportive learning environment. The district has earned designations as an A-rated district with 18 schools of excellence and two national blue ribbon awards under superintendent Dr. Shane McCord’s leadership, according to the official website.
The next steps or further actions from this meeting were not detailed during this session.
